93
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, February 10, 2014/Magha 21, 1935 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Coal; Corporate Affairs; Drinking Water and Sanitation; Earth
Sciences; Human Resource Development; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and
Renewable Energy; Rural Development; Science and Technology;
Water Resources; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Schemes for destitute/neglected
children
*261. SHRIMATI RAJANI PATIL:
Will the Minister of  WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of destitute/neglected
children in the country;
(b) the details of schemes/programmes
in existence for protection/education of such
children;
(c) whether Government has reviewed
these schemes/programmes in the recent
past;
(d) if so, the details along with the
outcome thereof; and
(e) the steps proposed to be taken by
Government to make these schemes more
purposeful?
Implementation of Sachar Committee
recommendations
*262. SHRI K.C. TYAGI: Will the
Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has reviewed
the progress on the action taken by various
Departments/States/UTs/agencies/
authorities on the recommendations made
by the Sachar Committee for ameliorating
the condition of minorities and if so, the
details thereof; and
(b) whether Government has laid down
any time-frame for implementation of the
recommendations and if so, the details
thereof?
Utilization of funds under the
Nirbhaya Scheme
*263. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has utilized
the funds meant for implementation of the
Nirbhaya Scheme, if so, the details thereof;
and
(b) the details of the projects under this
scheme to protect the interest of women in
the country?
Progress of schemes and programmes
*264. SHRI MOHAMMED ADEEB:
Will the Minister of  MINORITY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:

94
(a) the details of schemes and
programmes of the Ministry which have
not yielded the desired results and the
reasons therefor; and
(b) the steps taken to plug the
loopholes?
Audit of private companies by
Government auditor
*265. SHRI K.N. BALAGOPAL: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any court verdict
that empowers the Government auditor to
audit books of accounts of private
corporate entities and if so, the details
thereof; and
(b) Government's stand on this issue?
Functioning of the Central Waqf
Council
*266. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the
Minister of  MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Waqf Council
has started functioning under the amended
Waqf Act;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken to make full
use of the provisions of amended Waqf  Act?
Performance of MGNREGA
*267. SHRI T.M. SELVAGANA-
PA THI: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the performance of
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural
Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
has been declining since its peak in
2009-10;
(b) whether Government has not been
active in promoting MGNREGA;
(c) whether Government's less interest
in MGNREGA has become an impediment
to the State Governments in implementing
it; and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to revive MGNREGA?
Dams in North Eastern Region
*268. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES  be pleased to state:
(a) whether either dams or mega dams,
which are being constructed or proposed
to be constructed in the North Eastern
Region have been given any clearances by
the Ministry in parallel with the Ministries
which control various regulatory
responsibilities;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of specific measures being
taken by NHPC on the design for structure
of Lower Subanshiri Hydro Power Project
at Gerukamukh in Lakhimpur district of
Assam by involving the Bureau of Indian
Standards (BIS), the Building Materials
and Technology Promotion Council
(BMTPC), The National Disaster
Management Authority (NDMA) and
similar other organizations?
Shortage of water
*269. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the
Minister of  W ATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of the prediction of
acute water shortage in the country by
2050, Government has since worked out
any strategy to deal with inefficient water

95
consumption pattern and if so, the details
thereof; and
(b) whether Government proposes to
have detailed discussions with the State
Governments and to find out a mechanism
to deal with the impending water crisis and
if so, the details thereof?
Allocation of coal blocks
†*270. SHRI THAAW AR CHAND
GEHLOT: Will the Minister of  COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that the Attorney General has accepted
in the Supreme Court that the process of
coal block allocation was not up to the mark;
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, February 10, 2014/Magha 21, 1935 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Coal; Corporate Affairs; Drinking Water and Sanitation; Earth
Sciences; Human Resource Development; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and
Renewable Energy; Rural Development; Science and Technology;
Water Resources; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 155
Supply of inferior coal
1867. SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN
IRANI: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether complaints of supply of
inferior quality/sub-standard coal, high
costs of transportation, irregular supply
etc., have been received from power
companies/thermal power plants and other
consuming units in the country including
in backward areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the nature of such complaints, company-
wise; and
(c) the action contemplated/being taken
to address these issues?
Supply of coal to power plants in
Rajasthan
1868. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has assessed
the existing requirement of coal for power
plants in Rajasthan;
(b) if so, whether the required quantity
is being supplied to those power plants in
the State;
(c) if not, the reasons for inadequate
supply of coal to those power plants; and
(d) the steps taken by Government in
this regard?
Import of coal
1869. SHRIMATI W ANSUK SYIEM:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Coal India Ltd. (CIL)
has been mandated to meet the fuel supply
gap for power producers through import
of coal;
(b) if so, whether any of the major
power producers have placed their indents
to CIL for import of coal; and
(c) whether foreign coal producers/
traders prefer to deal with power producers
in India directly rather than dealing with
CIL which has no expertise or mechanism
in handling bulk coal imports?

498
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Cancellation of coal blocks
†1870. SHRI NARESH AGRAWAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
cancel the 61 coal block allocations which
have not obtained the approval of the
Ministry of Environment and Forests;
(b) if so, the loss of revenue incurred so
far by Government from these coal blocks
since the allocation of coal blocks; and
(c) the action Government proposes to
take against the companies which have not
started the task of exploration and mining
in the coal blocks on time?
Transfer of coal mining areas of
GIPCL
1871. SHRI BHARATSINH
PRABHATSINH PARMAR: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Gujarat
Government has recommended 7830.77
hectares area for under ground coal
gasification mining lease of Gujarat
Industries Power Company Ltd. (GIPCL)
to the Ministry;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government has recommended a block of
2300 hectares area only; and
(c) if so, by when the remaining area
would be recommended to GIPCL?
Coal for thermal power projects in
Rajasthan
†1872. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
shortfall in the availability of coal for the
thermal power projects of Rajasthan;
(b) if so, the scheme chalked out by the
Central Government for the supply of coal;
(c) whether the Central Government is
contemplating to increase the annual
contracted quantum of coal for the thermal
power projects of that State as per their
need; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, if not, the
reasons therefor?
Allocation of coal from SECL to
Gujarat
1873. SHRI BHARATSINH
PRABHATSINH PARMAR: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the reasons for allocating coal to
Gujarat from the Southern Eastern Coal
Belts;
(b) what are the criteria of coal allocation
from the Western Collieries Ltd. (WCL);
(c) what action have been taken by
Government to allocate coal from the WCL
to the State; and
(d) whether Government is considering
allocate full subsidy to the State to
compensate additional financial
implications on account of import of
additional coal for power generation?
Gap between demand and supply of
coal
1874. SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN
IRANI: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) the production, demand and supply
of coal during each of the last three years of
Eleventh Five Year Plan, State-wise and
sector-wise;
(b) the reasons for shortfall in
production and supply vis-a-vis the targets
fixed during the said period and the action

499
plan contemplated to meet the shortfall
during the Twelfth Five Year Plan;
(c) whether Government has imported
coal to bridge the gap between demand and
supply of coal; and
(d) whether the recommendations of the
Inter-Ministerial Task Force for
rationalization of the existing coal sources
and supply of coal have been implemented
and if so, the details thereof and if not, the
reasons therefor?
Cancellation of coal blocks
